message:
Marcus, Priya, Tomas, first vertical mode mass and stiffness suit a 40 m steel deck and set damper size. Deck moves like full bus load on stiff spring, then numbers deciding are modal stiffness calculation (E11) with 20000 kg modal mass, about 286 body weights, giving 2.85 MN per m at 1.90 Hz.

Placing Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, secondary mass tuned to bridge mode) at midspan where mode shape peaks gives maximum effect with just-below tuning. Small extra weight tames large deck motion, then numbers deciding are Den Hartog optimum re-check (E54) with 1.85 Hz and 0.0956 damping ratio, and resonant response simulation (E47) falling from 1.75 m per s squared, about 0.178 times gravity and strongly felt, to 0.103 m per s squared, barely felt, factor 17 reduction.

Static sag plus shake fits below deck and dense crowd stays comfortable. Fist-height sag plus thumbnail shake is hand-width travel, violent becomes gentle bus braking, then numbers deciding are static sag calculation (E55) of 72.3 mm plus dense-crowd stroke scaling (E53) of 20.1 mm giving total compression calculation (E56) of 92.4 mm fitting below deck, and TMD-controlled acceleration scaling (E52) of 0.545 m per s squared, 0.0556 times gravity, below 1.00 m per s squared bound in Experimental and Numerical Study on Dynamics of Two Footbridges (E38). Ready, because modal scale, tuning, travel and comfort close jointly.
